summary:
**Conversation Overview**

The person asked for a list of open-source LLMs available on Hugging Face or similar hosting platforms, specifically pre-instruction-tuned base models. Claude provided a detailed list including Qwen3 235B-A22B, DeepSeek V3/R1, Llama 4 Scout/Maverick, GLM-4.7/5.2, Kimi K2.6/K3, Mistral Large 3, Gemma 3, and Phi-4/Phi-4-mini, along with practical notes on identifying base vs. instruct variants on HuggingFace, precision considerations for fine-tuning, and serving runtimes including vLLM, Ollama, and TGI.

The person then clarified their use case: they are building a new machine intelligence (MI) system that uses a compressed English-based token system internally. This MI is currently in early development, still at a factoid and definitions stage with weak conversational naturalness, and has been using existing AI systems as co-builders and directed coders. The LLM is intended to serve purely as an articulation and prediction interface — a natural language rendering layer — for this separate system, not as an independent reasoner. Claude raised honest epistemic flags about unverifiable claims regarding the alternate system's nature, then reframed the problem as a standard sequence-to-sequence style transfer task and recommended smaller, fluency-optimized models (Qwen3-8B/14B, Llama 3.1-8B-Instruct, Gemma 3 12B, Phi-4-mini) combined with LoRA fine-tuning on paired compressed-to-fluent examples as the practical path forward.

The conversation ended with an unrelated question about the game Valheim, specifically how to obtain Tar. Claude explained that Tar is harvested from Tar Pits in the Plains biome by killing Growths and draining the pit, and noted its uses in crafting Darkwood building pieces, the Black Metal Chest, and the Hot Tub. The person's interests appear to span ambitious technical research projects and gaming.

Tar comes from **Tar Pits** in the Plains biome — dark, unexplored-looking pools scattered around the map.

- **Kill Growths** — slimy poison creatures that guard tar pits (best fought at range with a bow; they're nasty in melee). Growths respawn two at a time about an hour after being killed.
- **Drain the pit** — dig a trench from the tar pit down to lower ground to drain it out. Once sufficiently drained, you can harvest Tar nodes by hand — small nodes give 4 Tar, big nodes at the bottom give 15, and a single pit holds 69–108 Tar total.
- A common trick: put on an Eikthyr blessing for speed, lure a nearby Fuling camp into the tar pit so they clear out the Growths for you, then drain and collect.

Bring anti-poison resistance (mead or a Swamp-tier potion) since Growths and the tar itself both poison you on contact. You'll want it for Darkwood building pieces, the Black Metal Chest, and the Hot Tub.


Vanilla answer: just scroll the mouse wheel backward while steering — boats let you zoom out much farther than you can on foot, so keep pulling the camera back past where it'd normally stop. If the sail's still blocking your view, tilt the camera off to the side or go semi-top-down so you can see around it rather than straight over the bow.

Vanilla has no dedicated "boat zoom" setting beyond that — if you want it automatic, there are BepInEx mods for it: **CameraTweaks** or **Customizable Camera** let you set a separate max zoom distance specifically for when you're piloting a ship, and **ShipToShoreCam** auto-zooms out the moment you board and back in when you disembark.

Vanilla answer: just scroll the mouse wheel backward while steering — boats let you zoom out much farther than you can on foot, so keep pulling the camera back past where it'd normally stop. If the sail's still blocking your view, tilt the camera off to the side or go semi-top-down so you can see around it rather than straight over the bow.

Vanilla has no dedicated "boat zoom" setting beyond that — if you want it automatic, there are BepInEx mods for it: **CameraTweaks** or **Customizable Camera** let you set a separate max zoom distance specifically for when you're piloting a ship, and **ShipToShoreCam** auto-zooms out the moment you board and back in when you disembark.

Right, no mods on console. On Xbox, zoom is the **right stick** — click/push it (or it's mapped to right stick vertical movement in some control schemes) to pull the camera back. If that's not doing it, check the in-game control bindings menu since Valheim's console camera controls got remapped a couple times across updates — worth a quick look at your current bindings to see exactly which stick input is "zoom" on your version.

Console doesn't have the boat-specific auto-zoom mods since those need BepInEx (PC-only), so you're stuck manually pulling back every time you board, same as everyone else on Xbox has been complaining about.
